course_name_original: Disseny per a Fabricació i Muntatge
prerequisites: EM1012 - Mecànica de Màquines i Estructures
EM1015 - Ciència i Tecnologia de Materials
EM1019 - Elasticitat i Resistència de Materials
EM1020 - Teoria de Màquines i Mecanismes
EM1028 - Màquines i Instal·lacions de Fluids

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to know and participate in a team in the development of integrated work applied to the field of manufacturing engineering.
Ability to know and solve cases and problems related to manufacturing engineering.
Correctly use basic manufacturing technical terminology in English.
Ability to know and autonomously obtain, select, contrast, and synthesize information related to manufacturing engineering, as a basis for self-learning.
Ability to know and analyze product and part designs to redesign them according to manufacturing feasibility criteria.
Ability to know and select and evaluate design alternatives and forming processes justifiably and reasonably, using design for manufacturing and assembly methodologies and tolerance analysis.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Design for manufacturing and assembly in the product design and development cycle.
Thematic Block II. Design considerations for joining and assembly.
Topic 2. Assembly analysis. Design for assembly.
Thematic Block III. Design considerations for manufacturing.
Topic 5. Design for plastic deformation forming.
Topic 6. Design for sheet metal forming.
Topic 7. Design for chip removal forming.
Topic 8. Design for plastic parts forming.
Thematic Block IV. Functional dimensioning. Tolerances in design and manufacturing.
Sessions 1, 2, 3 and 4 - Computer-aided tolerance analysis: Tolerance accumulation and distribution.
Sessions 5 and 6 - Computer-aided tolerance analysis: Tolerance chains considering orientation tolerances.
Session 7 - Computer-aided tolerance analysis: Fixed and floating assemblies.
teaching_methods: Lecture. Theory sessions with explanation of main theoretical contents by the faculty.
Exercise and problem solving. Practical sessions (problems) with explanation by the faculty of the main procedural approaches to develop valid solutions for different problems and practical cases.
Problem-Based Learning (PBL). Practical sessions (problems) in which the faculty will present a specific problem or case for students to solve.

Laboratory work. Laboratory sessions in which students must apply different aspects related to the course contents using machines and equipment available at university facilities or specific software applications.

assessment_methods.method: Academic work completion, submission, and oral presentation
Laboratory practical work completion and submission

assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain at least 5 out of 10 points in the overall average grade. For the first and second calls, the final exam has a minimum grade of 4 out of 10; if this minimum is not achieved, the final grade will be the exam grade. Academic work (10%) is not recoverable, while laboratory practical work (30%) can be recovered in the second call. Fraudulent actions in continuous assessment activities will result in 0 points for the entire activity, and fraud in the final exam will result in a failing grade (0 points) for that call.
